name: Corinthian hexastyle temple on a podium (Capitolium type)
license: original procedural geometry (TIMELINES Studio); materials use CC0 Poly Haven textures, see data/textures/LICENSES.json
source: procedural bpy generator tl_buildings.py / tl_nature.py (via build_assets.py)
historical_accuracy_notes: Column height 10 lower diameters, eustyle intercolumniation (2.25 D, 3 D at the centre) and pediment rise of 1/9 of the front follow Vitruvius Book III; Corinthian capital height = 1 D (Book IV.1). v2 (2026-11-26) models attic bases, shafts with 24 flutes and entasis (straight lower third, taper to 5/6 D), capitals approximated by a bell with two rows of eight leaf patches, four corner volutes and a concave abacus with fleurons (an approximation, not carved acanthus), an entablature with three-fascia architrave, frieze, dentils, modillions, corona and sima, raking cornices, recessed tympanum, acroterion plinths, podium mouldings, bronze-doored cella. ESTIMATES: podium height (3.2 m), moulding profiles, entablature height (2.45 D), dentil/modillion spacing, 24 flutes (usual for Roman Corinthian shafts).
references: Vitruvius, De architectura (c. 30-15 BCE), Book III (temple proportions, eustyle) and Book IV (Corinthian order)
Maison Carree, Nimes (pseudoperipteral hexastyle Corinthian temple, c. 2 CE)
